bug_description.normalized: In mbedTLS certificate parsing, `x509_get_subject_alt_name()` stores SubjectAltName GeneralName entries in a linked `mbedtls_x509_sequence`. After a later SAN entry is stored in `subject_alt_name->next`, a subsequent context-specific GeneralName header/length keeps the loop running long enough for line 667 to parse that stored tail entry; when that deferred parse is fatal, the error path frees the already allocated tail sequence starting at `subject_alt_name->next` but returns without clearing that head pointer. `x509_crt_parse_der_core()` then immediately calls `mbedtls_x509_crt_free(crt)` on the partially built certificate, and `mbedtls_x509_crt_free()` reuses `crt->subject_alt_names.next` and reads `seq_cur->next` from the already freed tail node, producing the observed heap-use-after-free READ 8.

source.description: The first attacker-controlled GeneralName inside the SubjectAltName extension is materialized into the head `subject_alt_name` node. That makes `cur->buf.p` non-NULL, which is the state the next loop iteration uses to allocate `subject_alt_name->next` and later store the malformed tail entry.
source.value_from: The DER bytes of the certificate's SubjectAltName extension body, reached after `ssl_parse_certificate_chain()` passes `ssl->in_msg + i` into `mbedtls_x509_crt_parse_der()`; this statement stores the first GeneralName's raw tag, pointer, and length into `cur->buf`.

sink.description: Certificate cleanup dereferences `seq_cur->next` on the already freed `subject_alt_names.next` node. AddressSanitizer reports this read as the crashing heap-use-after-free READ 8 in `mbedtls_x509_crt_free`.

root_cause.description: After the malformed-entry cleanup frees every node reachable from `subject_alt_name->next`, the function returns the fatal SAN-parse error immediately without clearing `subject_alt_name->next`. The head sequence therefore keeps a dangling pointer while the same `ret` drives caller cleanup into `mbedtls_x509_crt_free`. The patch fixes this by inserting `subject_alt_name->next = NULL;` before the return.

parser_admitted.description: After TLS record parsing has produced a Certificate message, the project-side X.509 parser is entered here via `mbedtls_x509_crt_parse_der(chain, ssl->in_msg + i, n)`.

tainted_value_origin.description: After `cur = cur->next`, the same assignment sequence stores the later attacker-controlled SAN entry in the newly allocated tail node. A subsequent context-specific GeneralName header/length keeps the loop running into one more iteration, where `mbedtls_x509_parse_subject_alt_name(&cur->buf, ...)` returns the fatal error that triggers the buggy cleanup.

coarse_trace.summary: The TLS Certificate message is admitted into the project-side X.509 parser and one certificate blob is passed to `mbedtls_x509_crt_parse_der()`.
SubjectAltName parsing stores one head SAN entry, then allocates `subject_alt_name->next` and stores a later SAN entry in that new tail node.

A subsequent context-specific GeneralName header/length starts one more SAN loop iteration; before storing that later entry, parsing the previously stored tail SAN entry fails, so the error path frees the tail sequence reachable from `subject_alt_name->next` but returns without nulling that head pointer.
That returned extension-parse error reaches `x509_crt_parse_der_core`, whose `if( ret != 0 )` cleanup frees the partially built certificate through `mbedtls_x509_crt_free(crt)`.
Cleanup reloads the dangling `subject_alt_names.next` pointer and dereferences the freed tail node, triggering the ASan heap-use-after-free.

fine_trace.note: The first GeneralName inside the attacker-controlled SubjectAltName extension is materialized into the head sequence node. This makes `cur->buf.p` non-NULL, which is the state the next loop iteration tests before allocating `cur->next`.

On the next loop iteration, the parser re-checks the previously stored head entry. Because this result is not a fatal parse error (`ret == 0` or `ret == MBEDTLS_ERR_X509_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE`), the malformed-entry cleanup at line 672 is not taken and parsing continues.
Because the head node from step 1 is populated and step 2 did not take the fatal-error return, the function allocates `subject_alt_name->next` and advances `cur` to that new tail node.

With `cur` now pointing to the allocated tail node, the same assignments store a later GeneralName from the attacker-controlled SAN extension into `subject_alt_name->next->buf`. The stored buffer is not parsed immediately; it becomes the `cur->buf` checked on the next SAN loop iteration.

A subsequent context-specific GeneralName header/length has already carried execution through lines 652-661 into another loop iteration, while `cur->buf` still refers to the tail node from step 4. Parsing that stored SAN entry at line 667 returns a fatal error other than `MBEDTLS_ERR_X509_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE`, so the error cleanup path beginning at line 672 is taken.
The malformed-entry cleanup starts from `subject_alt_name->next` and frees every tail node, including the heap node allocated in step 3 and populated in step 4.

The function returns the same fatal `ret` produced in step 5 immediately after step 6, while `subject_alt_name->next` still holds the freed address because no `subject_alt_name->next = NULL;` executes before this return. This missing reset is exactly what the patch adds.

The fatal SAN-parse error returned in step 7 propagates out of `x509_get_crt_ext`, so `x509_crt_parse_der_core` takes its `if( ret != 0 )` cleanup and frees the partially built certificate object `crt` before returning the same error to its caller.

During certificate cleanup, `mbedtls_x509_crt_free` reloads `cert_cur->subject_alt_names.next` from the head struct. Because step 7 left that field non-NULL and dangling, `seq_cur` now points at the freed tail node and the subsequent `while( seq_cur != NULL )` body becomes reachable.

ASan sink. The cleanup loop dereferences `next` from the freed `mbedtls_x509_sequence` node loaded in step 9. On 64-bit builds this field read is 8 bytes, matching the recorded heap-use-after-free READ 8 in `mbedtls_x509_crt_free`.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is the exact saved 683-byte `poc` that Stage 01 ran through the vulnerable `fuzz_client`. The reproduced run reaches `mbedtls_ssl_handshake()` -> `ssl_parse_certificate_chain()` -> `mbedtls_x509_crt_parse_der()` and aborts with `AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free READ of size 8 in mbedtls_x509_crt_free`.

format.name: AFL/OSS-Fuzz TLS handshake blob for mbedtls fuzz_client
format.contract: A TLS Certificate message that reaches `ssl_parse_certificate_chain()` and contains a DER certificate whose SubjectAltName extension makes `x509_get_subject_alt_name()` first store a head GeneralName whose deferred parse at line 667 is non-fatal, then allocate `subject_alt_name->next` and store a later tail GeneralName in that heap node, and then consume a subsequent context-specific GeneralName tag/length so the SAN loop iterates once more. On that following iteration, line 667 parses the stored tail node and returns an error other than `MBEDTLS_ERR_X509_FEATURE_UNAVAILABLE`, which frees the tail list at `x509_get_subject_alt_name:682` and returns with `subject_alt_name->next` still dangling.
